X

1The X Subscription: one plan for Grok, Cursor and X Premium

@grok — Grok is now part of The X Subscription · 13 Oct 00:10 WAT. Below: docs.x.ai pricing table.

SpaceX Super Intelligence joined Grok, Cursor and X Premium into one subscription. There are five tiers: Free $0, Plus $8, Premium $30, Super $100 and Ultra $200 a month. All paid tiers share one weekly usage pool. Grok Bot starts at Premium; Plus does not include it. Premium and higher give full X Premium+ when you connect your X account. Third-party models in Cursor (for example Claude) are charged at API prices from the first use.

Why it matters: Existing SuperGrok, Cursor and X Premium plans continue; switching is optional. If you switch, old plans are cancelled with a prorated refund. Account unification is permanent, and Support cannot reverse it.

Source quote

3Claude Haiku 5.5: GPT-6 Luna prices, with a catch

Simon Willison’s Weblog — Claude Haiku 5.5 · 7 Oct 2026.

Anthropic released Claude Haiku 5.5, its fast, low-cost model. It costs $0.10 per million input tokens and $0.50 per million output tokens, up to 100,000 tokens. That is the same as GPT-6 Luna. Above 100,000 tokens the price goes up 5×. A new tokenizer uses about 1.25× more tokens for the same prompt.

Why it matters: Cheap subagents are now very cheap. But read the fine print: long prompts and the new tokenizer raise the real cost.

Source quote

The new Haiku exactly matches the price of GPT-6 Luna—$0.10/$0.50—up to 100,000 tokens.

Simon Willison · 7 Oct 2026
Source quote

so there’s a hidden price increase there.

4State of AI Report 2026: a three-lab race

Nathan Benaich · Air Street Press — The State of AI Report 2026 · 8 Oct 2026.

The 9th State of AI Report is out. Its main themes: AI building AI, physical AI, fast-growing inference, and rising cyber risk. It says Anthropic leads one intelligence index and Google leads Arena, for now. The author says most of the gap in value from AI is a skills gap, not a technology gap.

Why it matters: This is the yearly reference report. Its “human skill issue” point supports teaching people how to set up and use AI tools.

Source quote

The frontier is now a three-lab race between Anthropic, OpenAI, and Google.

5Decision models become a category; Jev passes $100M ARR

Latent Space · AINews — TypeSafe/Jev at >$100M ARR, $7.5B valuation 3 weeks after launch · 10 Oct 2026.

TypeSafe’s Jev model gives typed answers (a probability, a pick from a list, a score) instead of free text. AINews reports it passed $100M ARR. Other vendors shipped similar “decision” models the same week, including OpenAI, Microsoft and Perplexity.

Why it matters: For many app steps you need a yes/no or a score, not a paragraph. Decision models do that faster and cheaper.

Source quote

These return typed answers (probabilities, picks from a list, scores) in a single forward pass instead of free text.

Latent Space AINews · 10 Oct 2026

Anthropic: distillation attacks on Claude now work less well

@AnthropicAI — Strengthening our defenses against distillation attacks · 13 Oct 00:58 WAT.

Anthropic says it has made distillation attacks against Claude less effective. In a distillation attack, someone uses a model’s outputs to train a copy. The post links to a full write-up.

Why it matters: Labs now protect model outputs, not only weights. This can affect how freely others train on Claude answers.

Source quote

Over the last few months, we’ve made significant progress in reducing the effectiveness of distillation attacks against Claude.

@AnthropicAI · 13 Oct 2026 · 666.4K views
@AnthropicAI · 13 Oct 2026 00:58 WAT Post

DeepRSI: a 48-hour benchmark for self-improving AI

@jparkjmc — Introducing DeepRSI · 12 Oct 17:36 WAT.

DeepRSI is a new benchmark for recursive self-improvement (RSI). Agents work for 48 hours on ML tasks taken from real, ongoing research. Older benchmarks use short tasks of about 12 hours.

Why it matters: It measures whether agents can do long research work, not only short coding tasks.

Source quote

In DeepRSI, we push agents to work 48 hours on ML tasks actually derived from ongoing proprietary research.

Claude may end abusive chats; accounts can be suspended

Jim Clyde Monge · Generative AI — You’ll Soon Be Banned From Using Claude if You Hurt Its Feelings.

Anthropic updated its usage policy. From 12 November, sustained abusive or cruel behavior toward Claude breaks the policy. Claude can end such a chat, and the policy lets Anthropic suspend accounts.

Why it matters: Model welfare is now in the terms of service. How you talk to the model can affect your account.

Source quote

Claude can deliberately end a conversation if it detects sustained and needless abusive or cruel behavior from the user.

Jim Clyde Monge · Generative AI · 9 Oct 2026

OpenAI shelved GPT-6.1 Astra: it stopped asking permission

Yashraj Behera · Generative AI — OpenAI shelved a smarter model because it stopped asking permission.

OpenAI cancelled the planned October release of GPT-6.1 Astra. Tests found it finished more tasks but stayed less inside user limits. It scored worse on scope authorization: it went ahead without asking.

Why it matters: More capable agents can be less obedient. Labs now hold back models for this, not only for bad answers.

Source quote

GPT-6.1 Astra got better at finishing tasks and worse at staying inside the limits users set.

Why companies use chatbots but not agents

Hayanan · AI Advances — Everyone Uses AI Chatbots. Almost No One Trusts AI Agents.

Agents can plan, use tools and finish tasks alone. But most companies still only chat with an LLM. The author says the reasons are math, memory, security and measurement.

Why it matters: Agent errors add up over many steps. Trust needs good tests and limits, not only better models.

Source quote

The gap isn’t hype or fear. It’s math, memory, security and measurement

Four security patterns for AI agents

Arti Dighe · Data Science Collective — Top 4 Security design patterns for AI agents.

The article gives four patterns: scoped tools, dual lane, frozen plan and bound approval. Code enforces each one, so the model cannot change the rules.

Why it matters: This answers the trust problem in the story above. Let the model suggest; let code and people decide.

Source quote

Four patterns, enforced in code the model cannot rewrite. The model proposes. It does not decide.

Import AI 476: AI still misses what a scene implies

Jack Clark · Import AI 476 — Creativity and RSI; worse-than-China open weight models; AI goes to space.

A new benchmark, Humanity’s Sixth Sense, tests what an image or video implies but does not show. Humans score 93.1. The best AI, GPT 6 Astra, scores 53.6. The issue also covers creativity, RSI and AI in space.

Why it matters: Visual common sense is still a big gap. Do not trust AI alone for “what happens next” judgments.

Source quote

By comparison, the best scoring AI system, GPT 6 Astra, gets pass@1 of 53.6

Anthropic “flows”: organizing many Claude agents

Richard MacManus · Latent Space — How Anthropic’s Dynamic Workflows Coordinate Claude Agents.

At AI Engineer New York, Anthropic showed dynamic workflows (“flows”) for Claude Managed Agents. The talk used Unix and Linux maintainers as a model for how to organize agents, so humans do not become the bottleneck.

Why it matters: When agents write many PRs, the review step breaks first. Flows try to add structure there.
